newsitem.title: CROATIA: PRESS DIGEST - Croatian weekly - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Croatian weekly - Aug 1.

text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian weekly Tjednik. Reuters has not verifired these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Interview with Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic on the eve of his meeting with Franjo Tudjman: "I want us to turn a new page in our relations, since they have not been too cordial for a long time...Croatia is for us the most important country. I would like to see Croatians feel their (international) border is the Drina river, while for Bosnians this would be the sea.

- Jewish Property in the pro-Nazi Independent State of Croatia (NDH) or Genocide as Business - Tjednik traces what happened to Jews and their property that Croatian fascists or Ustashas confiscated in WW 2.
- Analysis - Croatia under threat of sanctions -- by losing its political credibility, Croatia is now needlessly being treated in the same way as their Balkan neighbours in Belgrade.

- "Croatia is not a candidate for membership in the European Union as it has not met requirements for this... Croatia has not regulated its relations with Bosnia in accordance with the Dayton peace agreement," says a European Commission member Hans Van den Broek in an interview.
- Surprise retirement of Croatian army commanders who had made their names in the war begs question -- could it be that the authorities want to get rid of possible candidates for The Hague?

- "Now is the crucial time for Bosnia and Croatia. Two years have gone by since the war ended and we have a long way to go to make sure the peace process is being taken seriously. ...Tudjman's last statements show he now agrees with (U.S.) demands..but he has to keep his promises," says U.S. Assistant Secretary for Human Rights John Shattuck in an interview.

- Croats are being evicted from their flats in the Serbian town of Zemun, where authorities are in hands of radical Vojislav Seselj. A lawyer representing one of the evicted families says actions are condoned by Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557 075
